basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Et vidit Deus lucem quod esset bona. Non velut incognitam antea repente lucem videns'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text:
Et vidit Deus lucem quod esset bona. Non velut incognitam antea repente lucem videns laudavit, quia bonam dicit; sed eam quam laudabilem se facturum noverat, jam factam hominibus laude dignam ac mirandam esse declaravit. Verum quia non totas mundi tenebras luce infusa dispulit (hoc enim superni est saeculi fixa ac perpetua luce perfrui), sed ab una illum parte illustrans, aliam reliquit obscuram, recte subditur:

Et divisit lucem ac teneoras. Divisit namque eas non solum qualitatis, sed et locorum distantia, lucem videlicet in superiore orbis parte diffundendo, in qua humana erat conversatio futura, inferiora vero ejus priscis in tenebris remanere sinendo.
